messages:
maria-ramirez: quick check — we're seeing missing spans for the kv-cache async worker. API service has a trace that shows it enqueued the job, but in Jaeger/Tempo the worker child spans never appear. where should I look first? cc @kevin-cho

kevin-cho: first things: check the worker logs for traceparent/trace id propagation and confirm tracerprovider is set up before goroutines spawn. also check sampling config (OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER + OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG). can you paste the SDK init?

maria-ramirez: here's our python init snippet from the worker (simplified):
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, OTLPSpanExporter

trace.set_tracer_provider(TracerProvider())
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter()
trace.get_tracer_provider().add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
```

lee: looks okay at a glance. two common gotchas: 1) workers started by a process manager re-exec without env vars (missing OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT etc) 2) you might be dropping context when handing off to a new thread/process. are you using multiprocessing or launching new processes?

maria-ramirez: our queue consumer uses multiprocessing.Pool + a small wrapper. we do `pool.apply_async(worker_fn, args=(job,))` — so maybe context isn't propagated.

ashish: yup, multiprocessing won't carry thread-local context automatically. options: propagate trace id via job payload (traceparent header) or use OTEL instrumentation support to inject/extract at enqueue/dequeue. e.g. on enqueue: `inject(headers)` and on worker start: `ctx = extract(headers)` then `with tracer.start_as_current_span("worker"): ...`.

kevin-cho: also check sampling: if your SDK is defaulting to probabilistic low rate it may drop. try temporarily setting `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` (or parentbased(always_on)) on the worker pod to rule that out. I usually `kubectl set env deployment/kv-cache WORKER_OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on --namespace=prod` for a quick test.

observability-bot: FYI dashboards & runbooks:
- Traces dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/kvcache-traces/kvcache-traces
- Runbook: https://confluence.internal.redwood.com/display/OBS/Tracing+Worker+Missing+Spans
- Quick check list: `kubectl logs -l app=kv-cache -c worker --since=1h | grep -E "traceparent|trace_id"`

lee: another infra thing: if you have an Istio sidecar / proxy, check that the proxy isn't stripping the `traceparent` header. on istio we set `global.proxy.includeInboundHeaders=traceparent` in sidecar settings. also mTLS could cause header mutation.

maria-ramirez: good call. we do have istio. I'll check sidecar config and add explicit inject/extract in the job payload as a backstop.

kevin-cho: while you're testing, enable `OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the worker container to see exporter connectivity and sampling decisions. also tail the exporter logs: `kubectl logs deployment/kv-cache -c worker -f` and look for `SpanProcessor` export messages.

maria-ramirez: will try these. i've added a small change to propagate traceparent into the job body and set sampler to always_on temporarily. will report back in ~30m. thanks! :thumbsup:

ashish: if you want i can pair with you on the run later, could be faster to instrument extraction.

maria-ramirez: that would be awesome — ping me when free.

kevin-cho: great. if spans still missing after propagation + sampler, next step is to run a local reproducer with OTLP exporter pointed at the dev jaeger and tcpdump the traffic to ensure spans are sent.

observability-bot: note: tracing retention for traces-indexed is 7d in prod; for debugging you might want to push to staging jaeger with full retention if reproducing repeatedly.
